A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a two-level supply chain coordination framework, where a central planner coordinates the supply chain by setting a production plan, which is then followed by the individual plants in a decentralized fashion.
the proposed framework is able to coordinate supply channels and to make mediumterm lot size decisions in case of high setup costs, high service level requirements, and demand volatility.
the two-level logistics framework is capable to reduce the bullwhip effect in supply chains, to increase the service level and to reduce the inventory levels.

a supply network with a high degree of flexibility can significantly improve the ability to respond to demand fluctuations, and that the coordination of supply chains in a two-level framework can significantly improve the performance of a production network.
